item.title: Assembly Drill 2026-11-17: crackme
item.description:
# Crackme: find the input (Windows x64, arg in ecx)
``` check: movzx eax, cx ; 0F B7: low 16 bits, zero-extended shr ecx, 16 ; high 16 bits slide down cmp ecx, 0xC0DE jne fail add eax, ecx cmp eax, 0x11111 jne fail mov eax, 1 ret fail: xor eax, eax ret ```
`cx` is the low 16 bits (a "word") of `ecx`. `movzx eax, cx` copies that word into `eax` and fills the upper 16 bits with zeros. Which unsigned `x` (ecx) makes `check` return 1?
---
**Answer:** `x = 0xC0DE5033` (3235794995)
1. The function splits `x` into two words: `eax` = low half, `ecx` = high half (`shr 16` discards the low bits). The first `cmp` pins the high half to 0xC0DE. 2. Then low + 0xC0DE must equal 0x11111, so low = 0x11111 − 0xC0DE = 0x5033. The sum is 32-bit, so nothing wraps. 3. Glue the halves back together: high word 0xC0DE, low word 0x5033 → 0xC0DE5033.
